title: Scheme representability criterion for Weil restriction
statement: Let $S$ and $S'$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $p:S'\to S$ be finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Let $Z\to S'$ be a scheme over $S'$. Define a functor on $S$-schemes by $F(X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{S'}(X\times_SS',Z)$, with restriction by precomposition [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume that for every point $s\in S$, every finite subset of the underlying space of $Z\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is contained, via its natural map to $Z$, in an affine open subscheme of $Z$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-residue-field]. Then there exists an $S$-scheme $W$ and bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_S(X,W)\simeq F(X)$ natural in every $S$-scheme $X$. No quasi-compactness, separatedness or smoothness hypothesis on $Z$ is imposed.

source.place: BLR 7.6 Theorem 4, printed pp.194–195 (PDF pp.200–201), affine-neighbourhood criterion. Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf.

proof.text: The functor $F$ is a Zariski sheaf. Indeed, for an open cover $T=\bigcup T_a$, the schemes $T_a\times_S S\prime$ identify with the inverse images of $T_a$ under $T\times_S S\prime\to T$ and hence form an open cover. Compatible maps from them to $Z$ glue uniquely. Their composites to $S\prime$ agree with the projection on this cover, so uniqueness of gluing makes the glued map an $S\prime$-map. This proves precisely existence and uniqueness in the sheaf condition.

source.place: Tag 01JJ (lemma-glue-functors), condition (1); BLR 7.6 Proposition 3, written out for scheme-valued input.

proof.text: Index by all pairs $(V,U)$ with $V\subseteq S$ affine open and $U\subseteq Z$ affine open whose composite to $S$ factors through $V$; include the empty affine open. Define $F_{V,U}(T)\subseteq F(T)$ to consist of those maps for which $T\to S$ factors through $V$ and the map $T\times_S S\prime\to Z$ factors through $U$. Both factorizations, when they exist, are unique because they are through open subschemes; precomposition preserves them. The affine-chart lemma gives an affine $V$-scheme $R_{V,U}$ representing $T\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{S\prime}(T\times_S S\prime,U)$ on $V$-schemes. Viewed as an $S$-scheme, $R_{V,U}$ represents $F_{V,U}$: an $S$-map to it supplies exactly the required factorization through $V$ and the indicated $S\prime$-map. This verifies (2)(a) of the gluing criterion.

source.place: Tag 01JJ (lemma-glue-functors), condition (2)(a); affine construction of BLR 7.6 Theorem 4, proof, first paragraph.

proof.text: Fix an $S$-scheme $b:T\to S$ and $a:E=T\times_S S\prime\to Z$ in $F(T)$, and write $q:E\to T$. The map $q$ is finite by base-change permanence. The subset $C=|E|\setminus a^{-1}(|U|)$ is closed, so $q(C)$ is closed. Set $O_{V,U,a}=b^{-1}(|V|)\setminus q(C)$, an open of $T$. For any $f:T\prime\to T$, the bad set for the pulled-back map $a_f$ is the inverse image $C\prime$ of $C$ in $E\times_T T\prime$. The base-change image formula gives $q\prime(C\prime)=f^{-1}(q(C))$. Consequently $a_f$ lands in $U$ and $bf$ lands in $V$ exactly when $f(T\prime)\subseteq O_{V,U,a}$. A map with image in an open subscheme factors uniquely through it, by restricting its map of sheaves. Thus $T\times_F F_{V,U}$ is represented by this open subscheme. This verifies (2)(b), including arbitrary nonflat and nonreduced test schemes.

source.place: Tag 0BL4 (lemma-hom-from-finite-locally-free-representable), proof of condition (2)(b), with the base-change image check made explicit.

proof.text: For $t\in T$, put $s=b(t)$. The set $P=a(q^{-1}(t))$ is finite by finiteness of the fibres of $q$. Each point has a lift to $Z\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$: the corresponding point of $E_t$ maps to $Z$ and to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, so the fibre-product property supplies such a lift. Choose one for each element of $P$ and apply the hypothesis to this finite set; it gives an affine open $U_0\subseteq Z$ containing $P$. Choose an affine open $V\subseteq S$ containing $s$, and put $H=U_0\cap(Z\to S)^{-1}(V)$. Thus $P\subseteq H$. If $P$ is empty use $U=\varnothing$. Otherwise write $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and let $J=\{f\in A:D(f)\subseteq H\}$. This is an ideal since $D(f+g)\subseteq D(f)\cup D(g)$ and $D(rf)\subseteq D(f)$. The basic-open basis shows $J\not\subseteq\mathfrak p_x$ for every $x\in P$. Prime avoidance therefore gives $f\in J$ outside all these finitely many prime ideals. The basic open $U=D(f)$ is affine and satisfies $P\subseteq U\subseteq H$, so $(V,U)$ is an index from step 2. It follows that $t\in O_{V,U,a}$. Hence these opens cover $T$, and over each of them $a$ belongs to its corresponding $F_{V,U}$ by step 3. This is condition (2)(c).

source.place: Tag 0BL4 (lemma-hom-from-finite-locally-free-representable), proof of condition (2)(c); affine refinement by Tag 00DS (lemma-silly, prime avoidance) and Tag 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine).

proof.text: Steps 1–4 give all hypotheses (1), (2)(a), (2)(b), (2)(c) of the scheme-representability criterion. Apply it to $F$ and the family $F_{V,U}$. Its conclusion gives an $S$-scheme $W$ representing $F$, which means exactly the asserted bijections natural in every $S$-scheme. Every finiteness condition used above concerns $p$ and its base changes; no quasi-compactness, separatedness or smoothness assumption on $Z$ entered.

source.place: Tag 01JJ (lemma-glue-functors), conclusion; BLR 7.6 Theorem 4, final gluing argument.
